walkthroughs.body_html:
Photosynthesis & Plants — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Photosynthesis & Plants brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Photosynthesis & Plants.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT a limiting factor for photosynthesis?
options: Light intensity
CO₂ concentration
Temperature
Oxygen concentration
Plants only photosynthesise and do not respire; respiration is for animals only.
Plants gain most of their mass directly from sunlight, which has weight.
Yes — plants respire all the time to release energy; they also photosynthesise when there is light.
Plants only respire at night and only photosynthesise during the day; the processes never overlap.

mcqs.q: Where do plants get most of their biomass from?
options: Plants only respire at night and only photosynthesise during the day; the processes never overlap.
Plants get most of their mass from the soil through their roots.
Plants gain most of their mass directly from sunlight, which has weight.
From carbon dioxide in the air — the carbon in plant tissue comes mostly from CO2 fixed during photosynthesis.

mcqs.q: What drives water up the xylem in a tall tree?
options: Capillary action alone is enough to lift water to the top of any tree.
Plants only respire at night and only photosynthesise during the day; the processes never overlap.
Roots actively pump water up to the leaves like a heart.
Transpiration pull — evaporation from leaves creates tension that pulls water up the continuous water column.

5 units

mcqs.q: A student increases CO₂ concentration around a plant in bright light at 25°C and the rate of photosynthesis rises then levels off. At the plateau, which factor is most likely limiting the rate?
options: Light intensity or temperature
Carbon dioxide concentration
The amount of oxygen produced
The amount of starch in the leaf

mcqs.q: Which balanced symbol equation represents photosynthesis?
options: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂
C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O
6CO₂ + 6O₂ → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6H₂O
C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2CO₂ + 2C₂H₅OH

mcqs.q: A plant makes more glucose than it needs immediately. How is the excess usually stored in the leaf?
options: As starch
As glucose dissolved in the cytoplasm
As carbon dioxide
As lactic acid

mcqs.q: Why does the rate of photosynthesis fall above about 45°C?
options: The enzymes controlling it begin to denature.
There is too much carbon dioxide.
Light can no longer be absorbed.
The plant stops respiring.
